Build the Notifications.jsx page at d:\CareBridge AI\frontend\src\pages\patient\Notifications.jsx

This page shows patient notifications fetched from the real API.

API endpoints:
- GET /notifications/{patient_id} — returns array of { id, patient_id, title, message, notification_type, is_read, created_at }
- GET /notifications/{patient_id}/unread-count — returns { patient_id, unread_count }
- PUT /notifications/{notification_id} — body: { is_read: true } to mark as read

The user object from AuthContext: { _id, name, email, role, patient_id }

Page sections:
1. Header: "Your Notifications" with "Mark all as read" button
2. Summary cards (4): Unread count, by type counts (APPOINTMENT, HEALTH, SYSTEM, etc.)
3. Filter tabs: All, Unread, Appointments, Health, System
4. Notification list with:
   - Type icon (color-coded by notification_type)
   - Title, message, timestamp
   - Unread indicator (blue dot)
   - Mark as read button
   - Delete button (optional, just visual since patient can't delete)
5. "You're all caught up" footer when no unread
6. Loading skeleton, error state, empty state

Functionality:
- Fetch notifications on mount
- Mark individual as read via PUT API
- Mark all as read (loop through unread and PUT each)
- Client-side filter by type
- Format timestamps ("X minutes ago", "Yesterday", etc.)
- If no patient_id, show info message

Import api from '../../services/api'
Import { useAuth } from '../../context/AuthContext'
Import icons from lucide-react
Import './Notifications.css'

Also overwrite the CSS at d:\CareBridge AI\frontend\src\pages\patient\Notifications.css with a complete, beautiful, responsive design.

IMPORT AuthContext: import { useAuth } from '../../context/AuthContext';

Use useState, useEffect for data fetching. Include loading skeletons, error handling.

This page shows all hospitals fetched from the API and allows searching.

API endpoints:
- GET /hospitals/ — returns array of hospital objects with fields: _id, name, type, city, address, phone, specialties (array), services (array), beds, emergency, rating, status, created_at
- GET /hospitals/search/by-city?city=xxx — search by city
- GET /hospitals/{hospital_id} — single hospital details

The page must have:
1. Header with title "Find a Hospital" and subtitle
2. Search bar that filters hospitals by name/city/type (client-side filter + server search by city)
3. Filter buttons: All, Open Now, Nearest, Top Rated (client-side)
4. Sort dropdown: Recommended, Nearest, Highest Rated
5. Hospital cards in a responsive grid showing:
   - Hospital icon
   - Name, type, city/address
   - Specialties as tags
   - Rating, status (Open/Closed badge)
   - Phone, emergency availability
   - View Details button and Directions button
6. Loading skeleton, error state, empty state ("No hospitals found")

This page shows the patient's complete health monitoring data. It must fetch REAL data from APIs.

The user object from AuthContext: { _id, name, email, role, patient_id }

API endpoints (all use patient_id):
- GET /health-profiles/{patient_id} — health profile (blood_type, allergies, chronic_conditions, medications, emergency_contact)
- GET /vitals/{patient_id}/latest — latest vitals (heart_rate, systolic_bp, diastolic_bp, spo2, temperature, blood_sugar, recorded_at)
- GET /vitals/{patient_id} — all vitals history  
- GET /health-records/{patient_id} — all health records (diagnosis, treatment, notes, doctor, record_type, created_at)
- GET /health-records/{patient_id}/latest — latest health record
- GET /health-alerts/{patient_id} — all alerts (alert_type, severity, message, created_at)
- GET /health-alerts/{patient_id}/summary — { total_alerts, high_alerts, status, message }

Page sections:
1. Header: "My Health" with health status badge (Normal/Alert from summary API)
2. Health Profile card: blood type, allergies, conditions, medications, emergency contact
3. Latest Vitals grid (5-6 cards): heart rate, BP, SpO2, temperature, blood sugar — each with value, unit, status indicator
4. Health Records section: list of records with title, doctor, date, type, diagnosis
5. Health Alerts section: list of alerts with type icon, severity badge, message, timestamp
6. Health Summary footer: last checkup date, total records, active alerts, vitals status

Handling missing patient_id: If user.patient_id is undefined, show an info card saying "Please complete your patient registration first."
